A vertical 9:16 photograph looking steeply down from a pedestrian footbridge onto a rain-soaked British city junction at night, the wet steel handrail of the bridge running across the very top of the frame, beaded with raindrops and out of focus. Below, the junction reads like a diagram. In the lower third a British ambulance in yellow-and-green chequered livery waits at the stop line, its blue roof beacons throwing cold blue pools onto the glossy tarmac, its lettering too small and rain-smeared to read. Just ahead of its bonnet a police motorcycle outrider in a hi-vis jacket and white helmet sits astride his bike, one gloved arm held straight up, palm out, toward the ambulance. Through the middle of the frame, on a diagonal from upper left to lower right, three long dark saloon cars sweep across the junction nose to tail, their roofs catching the orange light, their headlight beams smeared forward on the wet road. A traffic signal on its pole glows red at the left edge. Two sodium-orange street lamps hang high on the right and bloom into a drizzle haze; everything they do not touch falls to teal and green-black. Focus is on the outrider and the ambulance; the motorcade shows slight motion blur. Shot on CineStill 800T with a 35mm lens, red halation round every lamp and brake light, visible grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, a faint handheld tilt. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from almost ground level at the kerb of a British city junction at night in steady rain, the camera just behind and below a police motorcycle outrider. His raised black leather glove, palm out, fills the upper left of the frame, large, soft and out of focus, a rim of sodium-orange light along its fingers and the shoulder of his hi-vis jacket cut by the left edge. Past the glove, sharp in the middle of the frame, a British ambulance in yellow-and-green chequered livery sits stopped at a red light, its blue beacons mid-flash, its windscreen a dark slab with two faint figures behind it, its lettering lost in glare. Across the space between the glove and the ambulance, a dark saloon car slides through the junction from right to left as a long smear of black bodywork and white headlight streak, a second one following just behind it at the right edge. The lower half of the picture is wet tarmac a few centimetres from the lens, rain spattering in a puddle that holds broken vertical reflections of red, blue and orange. One sodium street lamp blooms high in the top right through the drizzle; the sky and shadows go teal-black. Shot on CineStill 800T with a 28mm lens at a wide aperture, red halation round the red signal and the beacons, coarse grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, slightly tilted as if handheld. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken with a long telephoto lens from the far side of a rain-wet British city junction at night, the whole scene compressed flat. The foreground is filled by the motorcade passing between the camera and everything else: the dark flank of a black saloon car sweeps across the bottom half of the frame as a motion-blurred slab of glossy paint and reflected orange streetlight, a second car's rear corner and red taillight just leaving the left edge. In the gap above the passing roofline, sharp and still, stands the held moment: a police motorcycle outrider in a hi-vis jacket and white helmet, side-on, his gloved hand raised flat toward an ambulance stopped close behind him. The ambulance's yellow-and-green chequered bonnet and blue beacons sit just right of centre, the blue light catching in the rain, its signage unreadable at this distance. A red traffic light glows above it. Behind, a queue of stopped headlights and a row of terraced shopfronts dissolve into a pale fog band, two sodium lamps blooming into the haze high in the frame, the night sky teal-green. Shot on CineStill 800T with a 200mm lens, focus held on the outrider's glove and the ambulance, red halation round the lights, heavy grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, rain visible as soft diagonal streaks across the frame. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 film photograph taken from the very back of a British ambulance at night, looking forward down the length of the patient compartment towards the cab and its windscreen. In the lower left foreground, out of focus and cut by the frame edge, a patient lies on the stretcher under a pale cellular blanket, an oxygen mask over their face, one arm still at their side. A tired paramedic in a dark green uniform kneels beside them in the middle of the frame, one gloved hand resting on the blanket, her head turned away from the patient to look forward through the cab. Beyond her, through the narrow gap between the two front seats, the windscreen fills the upper third: rain beading on the glass, a red traffic light blooming into the drizzle, the blurred red tail lights of a stopped queue of cars, and the silhouette of the driver's shoulder. Focus falls on the kneeling paramedic; the patient is soft and the windscreen view melts into haze. Light comes from a cold white overhead strip in the compartment, dimmed and greenish, while the red of the traffic light washes faintly along the ceiling and blue beacon spill flickers through the rear side window. Everything else drops to teal-black. Shot handheld with a slight tilt on a 35mm lens, CineStill 800T pushed two stops, red halation round the traffic light, visible grain, underexposed with lifted blacks. Her face has natural skin texture and the drawn look of a long shift, mouth closed. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 close photograph of an ambulance driver sitting at a red light at night in a British city in the rain, seen from the passenger seat across the cab. He is a heavyset paramedic in his forties in a dark green uniform with a hi-vis stripe, stubble, creases round his eyes, both hands gripping the bottom of the steering wheel, mouth shut tight, staring forward and slightly up at the light. He sits in the right half of the frame, his profile cut by the edge, with the rain-streaked windscreen filling the left side and the top of the frame. The only real light on his face is the deep red of the traffic light pouring through the wet glass, so one side of his face glows red and the other falls into teal shadow; a faint amber glow from the dashboard instruments catches his knuckles from below, and a pulse of blue from the ambulance's own beacons reflects off the wet bonnet. Through the windscreen, the wide red light and the smeared tail lights of the stopped traffic dissolve into raindrops on the glass, which are in sharp focus at the edge of the frame while the street beyond is soft. The background behind his head is the dark side window, raindrops catching orange from a sodium street lamp. Shot on a 50mm lens close to wide open, CineStill 800T, red halation round every light, heavy grain, underexposed, lifted blacks, a little handheld tilt. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 detail photograph inside the back of a British ambulance at night, low and close at the height of the stretcher. In the upper half of the frame, a paramedic's blue nitrile-gloved hand rests on the edge of a portable patient monitor clamped to the stretcher rail; the screen glows soft green with a heart trace, its numbers too blurred to read, and that green light is the main light on the hand and on the creased green sleeve above it. In the lower part of the frame, out of focus, a fold of pale blanket and the clear tube of an oxygen line curl away towards the corner. The second paramedic is only a soft shape in the background, half in shadow, leaning forward between the front seats. Behind them, small and high in the frame, the rain-covered windscreen glows with a single red traffic light and a band of stopped red tail lights, all of it blurred into round bokeh through the wet glass, and flashes of blue beacon light catch the edges of the cabinets. Focus is sharp on the gloved hand and the monitor's edge, falling away fast behind. The rest of the compartment sinks into teal-black, with a dim cold strip light overhead. Shot on a 35mm film camera, CineStill 800T, red halation round the distant light, visible grain, underexposed, lifted blacks, slightly off-level as if held by hand. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photorealistic still of a British TV news reporter doing a live piece to camera on a rain-soaked city pavement at night, framed from the chest up and placed in the right third of the frame, his shoulders angled slightly away from us and his head turned square to the lens. He wears a full charcoal knitted balaclava with no openings at all, a large white ring stitched around the whole face, and a solid red triangle stitched high inside the ring over his left eye, so it sits on the right side of the picture at about two o'clock; the mouth area is plain knitted wool. The balaclava tucks into the turned-up collar of a dark navy waxed rain jacket beaded with water, and his black leather gloves hold a plain black handheld microphone with a blank grey foam windshield just below his chin. He stands completely still and straight-faced, like any correspondent mid-sentence. The only key light is the cold white lamp on top of the news camera, hitting him from slightly left and falling off across the knit. Behind him, out of focus and filling the left two-thirds of the frame: an ambulance held at a red traffic light, its blue beacons smeared into soft flares, a police motorcycle outrider with one gloved hand raised, and the dark shapes of a motorcade of saloon cars sweeping through the junction with their red tail lights streaking. An orange sodium street lamp blooms high in the drizzle haze at the top of the frame. Fine rain is visible against the dark. Eye-level, a 50mm lens, focus on the reporter's mask and glove, the street behind softened. Shot on CineStill 800T, red halation around the lamps and beacons, visible grain, slightly underexposed with lifted teal-black shadows, a faint handheld tilt. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photorealistic night street photograph, taken from across a wide wet junction in a British city with a long telephoto lens that stacks the scene into flat, compressed layers. The bottom third of the frame is wet black tarmac smeared with long vertical red and blue reflections, and across it a dark saloon car from a politician's motorcade crosses in motion blur, cutting through the foreground. In the middle band, small and slightly left of centre on the far pavement, stands a lone TV news reporter in a pool of cold white light from his camera crew's lamp: a dark rain jacket, black gloves, a plain black microphone held to his chest, and a full knitted balaclava with no openings, a white ring stitched around the whole face and a red triangle over his left eye, on the right side of the picture at about two o'clock. He faces the lens, tiny, calm and upright, as if none of it is happening. Beside him and towering over him on the right, an ambulance sits stopped at a red traffic signal, its blue beacons flashing into the drizzle, while a police motorcycle outrider in a high-visibility jacket holds one gloved palm up at it and two more black saloons glide through the junction behind. Above them the frame rises into fog: two orange sodium street lamps blooming in the haze and the dim outline of tall terraced buildings fading to teal-black. Focus sits on the reporter's plane; the crossing car in front is soft. Shot on CineStill 800T pushed two stops, heavy grain, red halation around every point of light, underexposed with lifted blacks, the frame faintly tilted as if handheld from a traffic island. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photorealistic still from very low on a wet British city kerb at night, the camera almost resting on the gutter and looking up at a TV news reporter delivering a live report. The lower part of the frame is a rippling rain puddle catching the red of a traffic light and the blue of an ambulance's beacons, out of focus, with a black camera cable snaking through the water. The reporter stands in the left half of the frame from the knees up, rising tall against the night, gripping a plain black microphone with a blank foam windshield in a black gloved hand at chest height, his other gloved hand loosely at his side. He wears a long dark charcoal raincoat with the collar turned up and a full knitted balaclava with no openings, a white ring stitched around the whole face and a red triangle high over his left eye, so it sits on the right side of the picture at about two o'clock; the mouth area is plain wool. He looks down the lens with total composure. Over his right shoulder, high in the frame and softly blurred, a red traffic signal glows through the drizzle, beneath it the lit cab of an ambulance waiting at the line, and the headlights of a motorcade of dark saloon cars rake across the junction, a police outrider's raised gloved hand silhouetted against them. His face is lit from below and one side by the wet street's orange sodium glow, the other side dropping into teal shadow. A 28mm lens, focus on his mask and microphone, the background and the puddle both soft. Shot on CineStill 800T, red halation round the signal and beacons, visible grain, underexposed with lifted teal-black shadows, a slight Dutch tilt. Thanks.

A photorealistic vertical 9:16 night photograph taken from outside a moving dark saloon car, looking in through its rear side window, which is beaded and streaked with rain. Behind the glass sits an invented government minister in his late fifties: a heavy, fleshy face with pink blotchy cheeks and broken veins across the nose, small pale eyes under puffy lids, thinning sandy-grey hair combed flat across a shiny scalp, a soft double chin pressing over a tight white collar and a loosened burgundy tie. He holds a phone hard against his ear with his lips pressed shut and his jaw clenched, glaring at nothing, plainly furious about something small. His face sits in the upper right of the frame, cut by the black window pillar, half lost behind running water. Laid over him on the glass is the reflection of the street outside: the soft smear of an ambulance's blue beacon, a red traffic light blooming into the rain, and long orange streaks from a sodium street lamp. Focus is on the raindrops and his near eye; the rest of the car interior falls into teal-black. The lower half of the frame is the wet, dark door panel catching thin red and blue reflections. Shot handheld on CineStill 800T with a 50mm lens, slightly tilted, red halation round every light, visible grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, in the manner of Saul Leiter photographing through a rainy window. Thanks.

A photorealistic vertical 9:16 photograph inside the back of a dark ministerial car at night in the rain, taken from low on the far end of the rear seat with a 28mm lens, so the cream leather seat and a folded-down armrest fill the bottom of the frame. On the armrest, sharp in the foreground, sits a small open glass jar of bright yellow lemon curd with a silver spoon in it and a crumpled napkin. Further back on the left, slumped into the seat, is an invented minister in his late fifties in a rumpled navy wool suit: a round, jowly face with pores and razor rash along the jaw, a small shaving nick on his chin, pink-rimmed tired eyes, wispy grey hair combed over, a crooked burgundy tie. He presses a phone to his ear, mouth shut in a tight, sulky line, nostrils flared, eyes rolled up at the roof lining. His head sits in the upper third of the frame, cut by the left edge. Through the rain-streaked window behind him, out of focus, an ambulance's blue lights pulse beside a red traffic light, throwing a cold blue band across one side of his face while a passing sodium street lamp lays an orange sweep over the other; the rest of the cabin sinks into teal-black, with a faint warm glow from a reading lamp in the roof. Shot on CineStill 800T, red halation round the lights outside, visible grain, underexposed, lifted blacks, handheld and slightly crooked. Thanks.

A photorealistic vertical 9:16 night photograph from the driver's seat of a dark ministerial car stopped in the rain, looking forward and slightly up at the rear-view mirror. In the mirror, small and sharp in the upper middle of the frame, is the reflection of an invented minister in the back seat, a man in his late fifties with a broad pasty face, heavy bags under narrow grey eyes, a bulbous red-veined nose, thin straw-coloured hair plastered to his forehead with damp, and a fleshy neck squeezed by his collar. He has a phone clamped to his ear, lips pressed together, brow knotted, staring straight into the mirror with petty fury. Around the mirror the windscreen is sheeted with rain, and beyond it, soft and out of focus, a red traffic light and the flashing blue beacons of an ambulance held at the junction break into long streaks and blooms through the wet glass, the wipers frozen halfway across. In the soft lower foreground the chauffeur's black leather gloved hands rest on the steering wheel, lit only by the faint amber dashboard glow. Everything outside the light sources falls to teal-black; a sodium street lamp throws a warm orange wash across the top of the glass. Shot on CineStill 800T with a 35mm lens, focus on the mirror, red halation round the beacons and the traffic light, visible grain, underexposed with lifted blacks, a slight handheld tilt. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 handheld frame from the rear doors of a UK ambulance at night, looking forward down the length of the black stretcher toward the small hatch window and the driver's back. A male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform, blue gloves and surgical mask kneels over a grey-skinned older man in an oxygen mask, locked arms mid-compression. A female paramedic braced against white cupboards and a teal seat points at a heart monitor glowing green with a ragged trace, shouting behind her mask. Hard cold ceiling strip light, blue emergency light strobing through the hatch, rain streaks on the cab windscreen. Shot on 35mm Kodak Vision3 500T, slight motion blur from the swaying vehicle, heavy grain, slightly underexposed. Thanks.
Monitor in the foreground, low and tight

Vertical 9:16 tight close shot inside a speeding UK ambulance at night, camera low beside a portable heart monitor bolted to a white cupboard. In the soft foreground the monitor screen glows green with a fast, jagged, chaotic heart trace and blurred unreadable numbers. Behind it, in sharp focus, a female paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical mask stares at the screen, eyes wide, sweat on her brow, mid-shout, one blue-gloved hand gripping a grab rail. Past her shoulder a male paramedic pumps a bag-valve mask over an older man's face. Cold fluorescent top light, green monitor glow on her skin, a slash of blue strobe across the teal seat. 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, 35mm film grain, handheld. Thanks.
High overhead from the ceiling corner

Vertical 9:16 steep high angle from the ceiling corner of a UK ambulance racing through rainy night streets, looking down on an older man lying on a black stretcher mattress, his grey face under an oxygen mask, shirt cut open, defibrillator pads on his chest, straps loose. A male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform, blue gloves and surgical mask drives both hands into his chest, arms blurred with motion. A female paramedic, also masked, braces against the swaying wall, squeezing a bag-valve mask with one hand and holding a monitor lead in the other. Dropped gauze wrappers and tubing slide across the teal-green floor. Hard cold strip light from above, blue emergency light flaring through a side window, 24mm lens, 35mm film grain, underexposed, camera shake. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 film still at night, from inside the back of a UK ambulance, looking forward. Foreground, out of focus: the shoulder and surgical-masked profile of a female paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and blue gloves, twisted toward the front, mid-compressions over a grey-faced older man in an oxygen mask on a black strapped stretcher. Middle: white cupboards, a teal seat, and the small sliding hatch window into the cab, where the driver's hands grip the wheel. Through the hatch and the rain-streaked windscreen beyond: a red traffic light and a police motorcycle outrider in a hi-vis jacket and helmet, gloved palm raised flat at them. Hard cold strip light, green monitor glow, blue strobe on wet glass. 35mm, grain, underexposed, handheld. No readable text. Thanks.
In the cab, low between the seats on a wide lens

Vertical 9:16 cinematic night still from the cab of a UK ambulance, camera low between the two front seats, wide 24mm lens. Bottom of frame: the driver's hands strangling the steering wheel, knuckles pale, a sleeve of a plain dark-green uniform. The dashboard glows faintly. Top two-thirds: a windscreen streaming with rain, one wiper caught mid-sweep. Just beyond the bonnet, lit hard by the ambulance's headlights, a police motorcycle outrider in a soaked hi-vis jacket and white helmet stands astride his bike, one gloved hand held up flat, visor down, unmoved. Above him a red traffic light blooms through the wet glass, sodium-orange streetlamps smeared behind, blue emergency light flickering across the rain drops. Shot on 35mm film, heavy grain, underexposed, slightly tilted handheld. No readable text, no logos. Thanks.
Long lens down the whole length of the compartment from the back doors

Vertical 9:16 film still at night, telephoto 85mm view down the full length of a UK ambulance's patient compartment, shot from by the rear doors. Near the bottom, soft: the feet of an older man under a pale blanket on a black strapped stretcher. Mid-frame: two paramedics in plain dark-green uniforms, surgical masks and blue gloves, a man and a woman, both frozen and turned to stare forward, one hand still pressed to the patient's chest. At the far end, small and sharp: the bulkhead hatch window, and through it the rain-blurred windscreen, a red traffic light and a hi-vis police outrider with one gloved hand raised. The red light spills in and stains the white walls and cupboards red, cut by a blue strobe. Green monitor glow. 35mm grain, crushed shadows, handheld. No readable text. Thanks.

Photograph a rainy night from inside the back of a UK ambulance, looking forward through the small rectangular hatch window into the driver's cab and out through the windscreen. Foreground, soft and out of focus: a paramedic's shoulder in a plain dark-green uniform, blue-gloved hand, a teal seat edge, the green glow of a heart monitor. Through the hatch and the rain-streaked windscreen, sharp: a black chauffeured saloon crossing slowly inches ahead, lit hard by the ambulance headlights, rain slanting through the beams. In its rear window a man in his fifties in a dark suit shouts into a phone, never looking over. Blue strobe washing the cab. Vertical 9:16, 35mm lens, shot on Kodak Vision3 500T, heavy grain, underexposed, handheld. Thanks.

Photograph the view from the driver's seat of a UK ambulance stopped at a junction on a pouring wet night, low and wide, the steering wheel and the driver's gripping hands dark at the bottom of the frame, a glowing dash screen without text. Filling the windscreen, inches from the bumper: the long black flank of a chauffeured saloon gliding slowly across, its paint beaded with rain, the headlight beams blasting white across its doors. A wiper blade frozen halfway, half the glass clear, half smeared. Through the saloon's rear side window, a suited man in his fifties on the phone, mouth open mid-complaint, eyes down. A police motorcycle shape at the far edge. Sodium-orange streetlamps blooming in the fog. Vertical 9:16, 24mm, 35mm film grain, underexposed, gritty. Thanks.

Photograph through the rain-covered windscreen of an ambulance at night with a long lens, framed tight on the rear side window of a black saloon passing slowly across, a few feet away. Inside that window, a man in his fifties in a dark suit and loosened tie holds a phone to his ear, frowning, gesturing, absorbed, lit by a small warm reading light. Over the whole image, faintly reflected in the ambulance windscreen: the green trace of a heart monitor and a blue emergency strobe. Water droplets on the glass in sharp focus, raindrops streaking through white headlight glare, sodium-orange bokeh behind. Cold teal shadows, crushed blacks, 85mm, shot on 35mm Kodak Vision3 500T, coarse grain, slightly underexposed, handheld. Vertical 9:16. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 cinematic still, night, inside a stopped UK ambulance. In the sharp foreground, a wall-mounted heart monitor's dark screen shows one unbroken flat green line, its glow the brightest thing in frame; the small figures on it fall soft and unreadable. Behind it, out of focus on an 85mm lens, a male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical face mask leans over the black stretcher, blue-gloved hands resting motionless on an older man's chest, oxygen mask on his grey face. Hard cold ceiling strip light, blue emergency light sweeping across the white cupboards, rain beading on the rear window. Shot on 35mm film, real grain, slightly underexposed, quiet and still. Thanks.
The whole room after the fight

Vertical 9:16 cinematic still on 35mm film at night: the full rear interior of a UK ambulance, seen from the back doors on a wide 24mm lens, low and level. White walls and cupboards, teal-green seats, grab rails, and a black stretcher with straps down the centre, where an older man lies still, grey-skinned, oxygen mask on. A woman paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical face mask sits back on her heels, blue gloves lifted just off his chest; her male colleague, masked, stands frozen with one hand on the rail. On the side wall a monitor glows with one flat green line. Through the small hatch window, the driver's silhouette and pulsing blue light; rain streams down the windows. Hard cold ceiling strips, grain, underexposed, total stillness. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 cinematic close-up on 35mm film, night, inside a UK ambulance. Looking down at two blue-gloved hands, one laid over the other, resting still on the centre of an older man's chest over a thin pale gown, the pushing finished. At the top of the frame, his grey chin and the edge of a clear oxygen mask. One side of the frame is washed green by the glow of a heart monitor's flat line, reflecting off the gloves and skin; a slow band of blue emergency light falls across from a rain-streaked window. The black stretcher mattress and a loose strap fill the bottom of the frame. Hard cold overhead light, deep shadow, real grain, slightly underexposed. Quiet and devastating, not gory. Thanks.
